name: Kordiam
author: Kordiam

sections.description:
Kordiam is editorial planning software for newsrooms and content marketing teams. This plugin connects a Kordiam account to one or several WordPress sites and keeps the two in step: what the desk plans in Kordiam appears in WordPress, and what the site publishes shows up on the story lists in Kordiam.

Two ways of working are supported.

  • Planned content. A story is planned and given its meta-data in Kordiam. Kordiam creates the matching post in WordPress, and later changes on either side are synced.
  • Breaking news. A story starts as a post in WordPress. The plugin sends the relevant data to Kordiam so the story lists stay complete.

The following is kept in sync:

  • Slug and story description
  • Publishing date and time
  • Statuses, matched to WordPress post statuses you choose
  • Categories, matched to WordPress categories or to a custom field
  • Authors, matched by email address
  • Links back and forth between the two systems
  • Custom fields, both story-level and publication-level
  • Tasks and their assignees
  • Text, pictures, video and other files planned in Kordiam

Nothing is synced until you have said what maps to what. Every mapping has an explicit “do not import” option, and each of the ten settings screens is a plain two-column table: what Kordiam sends, and where it should go.

The plugin works with both the block editor and the classic editor. In either one, a panel next to the post shows the story description and a link straight to the story in Kordiam.

You need a Kordiam account to use this plugin. Teams of 15 or more users can request a free test account on the Kordiam website.

Relationship to the Desk-Net plugin

Desk-Net has been renamed Kordiam, and this plugin is the successor to the Desk-Net plugin. It is a separate plugin rather than an update, so nothing changes until you install it and switch over.

When you activate Kordiam on a site that has Desk-Net data in its database, the settings, mappings and story links are copied across automatically. The Desk-Net data is copied, never moved or deleted, so deactivating Kordiam and going back to Desk-Net leaves you exactly where you were.

Do not run both plugins at once. While the Desk-Net plugin is still active, Kordiam shows a notice and keeps its own sync switched off, so that a single story cannot be sent to Kordiam twice.

External services

This plugin connects to Kordiam, the editorial planning service it exists to integrate with. Without a Kordiam account the plugin has nothing to talk to and does nothing.

Traffic goes in both directions, and both directions are described below.

What this site sends to Kordiam

Requests go to https://kordiam.app. They are made when a post is created, updated, trashed or deleted, and when the plugin needs to look up your Kordiam configuration for a settings screen.

Depending on which mappings you have configured, a request can contain:

  • The Kordiam API credentials for your account, exchanged for a short-lived access token
  • The post ID, title and slug
  • The post’s public URL and its edit-screen URL on this site
  • The publishing date and time
  • The Kordiam status and category you mapped the post’s status and category to
  • The values of the post fields you mapped to Kordiam custom fields
  • The display name and email address of the post author, or of the user in a post field you mapped to a Kordiam task

What Kordiam sends to this site

Kordiam calls this site’s REST API to create, update and delete posts, and to upload files. To do so it authenticates with the API key and secret shown on the plugin’s “WordPress Credentials” screen. Those requests carry the story data planned in Kordiam — title, description, slug, status, category, dates, tasks, custom fields — and any files attached to a story, which the plugin adds to the media library.

Terms

  • Service: kordiam.io
  • Terms and conditions: kordiam.io/terms-and-conditions
  • Privacy policy: kordiam.io/website-privacy-policy
  • Data protection and GDPR, including the data processing agreement: kordiam.io/gdpr
sections.installation:
You need an active Kordiam account and its API credentials. Once you have an account, request the API credentials from support@kordiam.io.

  1. Install the plugin through the Plugins screen in WordPress, or upload its folder to /wp-content/plugins/.
  2. Activate it on the Plugins screen. If the older Desk-Net plugin is active, deactivate it first.
  3. A “Kordiam” entry appears in the admin menu, below Posts.
  4. Open it and work through the sub-pages to connect Kordiam to WordPress and set up the mappings.
  5. We strongly recommend reading this support article before changing the settings.
sections.faq:
Who is this plugin for?

Customers of Kordiam, the editorial management platform. It helps medium to large editorial and content marketing teams plan and coordinate content across several platforms.

Do I need to be a Kordiam customer?

Not to try it out: you can test Kordiam and the plugin for free. After the trial you need a paid Kordiam account.

I used the Desk-Net plugin. Do I have to set everything up again?

No. Activating Kordiam copies your Desk-Net settings, mappings and story links across. Deactivate the Desk-Net plugin first so the two do not sync the same story twice.

Can I go back to the Desk-Net plugin?

Yes. Kordiam copies the Desk-Net data instead of moving it, and never changes or deletes it. Deactivate Kordiam, activate Desk-Net, and the older plugin works as before.

What happens to my posts if I delete the plugin?

Posts, pages and media stay untouched. Deleting the plugin removes only its own settings, the links between posts and Kordiam stories, and its access-token table.
